case.pattern_description: A shared-device fraud pattern was identified, involving a single handset profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) and an anonymising proxy, which was used to make purchases on 28 different customers' cards in the same weeks, each time appearing as a new device with transactions of $74.96-$252.28. This pattern matched four confirmed closed cases that could not be mapped to any known typology. The fraud was discovered by tracing card -> transaction -> device -> card in TigerGraph.

sar.narrative: Customer C13487, holder of card C13487-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-15 20:30 and 2016-11-26 17:39, 3 transactions totalling $439.61 were made on the card online from device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' through an anonymous proxy: $112.37 (3460634, 2016-11-15 20:30), $74.96 (3478561, 2016-11-22 16:11), $252.28 (3489320, 2016-11-26 17:39). The same device profile was used on 28 other customers' cards in the same period, most of them behind anonymous proxies and each time as a new device, indicating a common actor. The activity is suspicious because: Device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' was used by 28 cards in a 60-day window around the alert; 28 of them behind an anonymous/hidden proxy and 28 flagged as a New device. 4 closed case(s) on cards that used this profile were confirmed fraud, 4 of them recorded as an undocumented pattern. It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-2971, CC-3035, CC-2649. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
